title: Off-Plan Buyers Check Your Past. What Will They Find?
notes:
Your buyers have a free tool on their phone. In one hour, it can tell them more about you than your entire sales gallery.

In this episode, Mario explains how off-plan buyers check a developer’s past before they believe the next project, and how developers can turn that hour into their best sales argument:

  • Why your next project is not sold by your next rendering, but by your last building
  • The burger-ad test: what happens when the promise and the delivery do not match
  • How to show your track record before buyers discover it alone
  • Why giving buyers real unit data tells them you are not afraid of the truth

title: Dubai Off-Plan: Correction or Crash? My Forecast
notes:
Dubai home sales fell 38% in the third quarter, prices sit about 10% below their peak, and the biggest supply wave in the city’s history is still coming. Is this a correction or a crash?

In this episode, Mario gives developers the full picture of the Dubai off-plan market, with real numbers and no hype:

  • What changed after the war started at the end of February, and why buyers became careful, not absent
  • Why almost 3 out of 4 homes sold are still off-plan
  • How prices are splitting: apartments down much more than villas
  • The 2027 supply question, where forecasts range from 60,000 to more than 160,000 units
  • Two opposite developer strategies: heavy discounts versus holding price and launching megaprojects
  • What S&P Global, UBS and Emaar’s founder expect

At the end, Mario shares his own forecast for the next six months, for 2027, and for the window that could open for patient buyers.

This episode is for information only and is not financial advice.

title: Presale Buyers Cannot Read Floorplans
notes:
You have beautiful renderings, stunning video tours and a professional brochure. And your buyer still asks: “But can I fit a king bed in this bedroom?”

In this episode, Mario explains why that question is costing off-plan developers sales. The problem is not visualization quality. It is visualization granularity: every unit, every room, the view from every window, correct and reliable.

You will learn:

  • Why a floorplan is to a normal buyer what an autopsy is to someone who is not a doctor
  • The information gap: why developers think they gave buyers everything, while buyers understand almost nothing
  • Why trying to answer every furniture and measurement question never works
  • How letting buyers walk through their own unit, not a demo unit, turns hesitation into signed contracts

Your buyers do not need a better picture of the dream. They need to walk into their own home.

title: Off-Plan Presale? 3 Rules Before Launch
notes:
Every branded residence launching in Miami looks the same. Same images, same mood, same promises, and buyers can’t remember which project was which.

In this episode, Mario shares the three rules every developer needs before launching an off-plan presale:

  • Never fake the visual. AI images are cheap and fast, and that’s the trap. Every image should trace back to the real plans, dimensions and materials.
  • Earn the click. Buyers scroll past generic hero images. They click on their floor, their view, their kitchen.
  • Show every unit, inch by inch. This is the one that matters the most. When buyers can see every unit in full detail, they stop imagining and start deciding.

You’ll also hear a simple test you can run today to see how your own presale stands out, and three questions to ask yourself before your next launch.

title: Every Unit Deserves the Penthouse Treatment
notes:
You made fifteen beautiful penthouse renderings. Now how do you sell the other 235 units?


In this episode, Mario explains why the hero-unit strategy backfires in presale. When buyers have to imagine how the penthouse translates to their one-bedroom, doubt sets in, and imagination is where deals die.


He tells the story of a developer who did the opposite: he visualized every unit with the same precision, from studios to penthouses. The result was that studios stopped feeling like a compromise and started feeling verified.


You’ll learn:


Why hero renderings create a credibility gap for the rest of the building

How complete certainty makes any unit feel premium

The shift from buyer suspicion to buyer choice, and why it drives sales velocity

The three questions developers always ask: premium positioning, cheapest-unit risk, and cost


Mario builds the technology behind this approach, and he says so openly. His experience spans ultra-luxury resorts, student housing, and multifamily projects from 100 to 2,000 units.

title: The Verification Gap
notes:
Your buyers can now compare your 2018 renderings with Google Street View in under a minute. Every developer has a gap between what they promised and what they built. The question is how big yours is.

In this episode, Mario Comando, co-founder of SuitesFlow, explains the verification gap: the distance between a developer’s renderings and the finished building. He walks through how smart off-plan buyers measure it, and why they’ll increasingly demand data instead of narrative.

You’ll learn:

  • The simple Street View exercise that reveals any developer’s track record
  • The six pieces of data buyers should ask for before signing
  • The red flags that show a developer isn’t ready to commit
  • Why this scrutiny is inevitable, and how developers can turn it into an advantage

It sounds like an episode against developers. It isn’t. It’s the hard truth most marketers won’t say out loud: the developers who win the next cycle will hand buyers the proof before they ask for it, then sell an even bigger dream on top of it.

title: Buy Risk, Sell Certainty: Where the Money Lives in Off-Plan Real Estate
notes:
Why do off-plan buyers make money before a building is even finished? Because price follows certainty.

In this first episode of TheRealFlow, Mario explains the core mechanic behind off-plan real estate. You enter at the riskiest moment, when the price is lowest. As construction moves forward, risk drops and value rises. Then you can assign your contract to the next buyer, without ever owning the property.

In this episode:
• Why price moves with certainty, not time
• How contract assignment works: you buy a right, not a property
• Why the developer has even more reason to deliver than you do
• A real example: $50,000 deposit, $100,000 gain
• What to check before you buy: developer track record, the price gap, legal and tax rules

"You buy risk. You sell certainty. That's where the money lives."
